findings.highlight: in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was
findings.evidenceJa: こんなあたしでも、きっと昔は、ピアノが大好きだったんじゃないかなってことを
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants to remember or recognize that even someone like her must surely have loved the piano once. The English produces a malformed past clause in which she was already certain then, erasing her present, tentative reconstruction of a lost feeling.
findings.japanese:
「ううん…
こんなあたしでも、きっと昔は、
ピアノが大好きだったんじゃないかなってことを」
findings.todokanai: "No… in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was."

findings.highlight: Somehow, I guess it's all working out
findings.evidenceJa: なんだか、どうでもよくなってきてるのかな
findings.explanation: After saying she once hated her mother, Kazusa wonders whether she is beginning not to care anymore. The English says the situation is working out, replacing emotional detachment or exhaustion with optimistic resolution.
findings.japanese:
「はは…あんなに嫌ってたはずなのにな。
なんだか、どうでもよくなってきてるのかな」
findings.todokanai: "Haha… Even though I hated her so much. Somehow, I guess it's all working out."

findings.highlight: an overbearing girl who easily misunderstands everything
findings.evidenceJa: 思い込みの激しい痛いコ
findings.explanation: Setsuna protests that they are making her sound like a painfully or embarrassingly deluded girl who commits intensely to assumptions. 'Overbearing' instead characterizes her as domineering toward other people, importing a different interpersonal fault.
findings.japanese:
「ふ、二人とも、馬鹿にしないでよ！
わたしのこと、思い込みの激しい痛いコみたいに言って」
findings.todokanai: "S-Stop making fun of me, you two! You're making me sound like an overbearing girl who easily misunderstands everything."

findings.highlight: my whole world is flipped upside down in an instant
findings.evidenceJa: 一瞬のうちにうやむやになってしまった
findings.explanation: Kazusa's interruption causes the preceding dispute or question to become muddled and left unresolved in an instant. The English invents Haruki's whole world being overturned and never states that the conversation has been dropped.
findings.japanese: そして、一瞬のうちにうやむやになってしまった。
findings.todokanai: And my whole world is flipped upside down in an instant.

findings.highlight: "…The Kanto region will have very cloudy skies during the day, and snowfall is expected during the night, primarily in the mountain range. Up next are the forecasts for each region in the country…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「続いて北関東地方、日中から雲が多く、
夜には山間部を中心に雪となるでしょう。
では各地のお天気です…」
findings.explanation: A broader Northern Kanto destination is narrowed in English.
findings.japanese:
「続いて北関東地方、日中から雲が多く、
夜には山間部を中心に雪となるでしょう。
では各地のお天気です…」
findings.todokanai: "…The Kanto region will have very cloudy skies during the day, and snowfall is expected during the night, primarily in the mountain range. Up next are the forecasts for each region in the country…"

findings.highlight: Haruki-kun really leaves nothing to chance
findings.explanation: Setsuna substitutes Haruki's name into 転ばぬ先の杖, 'a cane before a fall,' making him the preventative implement who is always prepared. The generic compliment about leaving nothing to chance deletes the proverb substitution and the joke's image.
findings.japanese: 「さすが、転ばぬ先の春希くん、だね」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun really leaves nothing to chance, huh?"

findings.highlight: close out the year-end party with a toast
findings.evidenceJa: 忘年会で言うところの『一本締め』の時間
findings.explanation: 一本締め is the ceremonial rhythmic hand-clap used to close a gathering, not a toast. The English replaces the named closing action with a different drinking ritual.
findings.japanese:
テーブルに並べられたご馳走は既に底をつき、
忘年会で言うところの『一本締め』の時間になった。
findings.todokanai: The feast that had been laid out on the table is already finished, and it's time for everyone to close out the year-end party with a toast.

findings.highlight: "That's just… terribly convenient for you. Utterly selfish and self-centered. You're completely disregarding your friend's and your boyfriend's personal thoughts on the matter. Can't you see how unbelievably egoistic that is?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「それってさ…勝手で、身勝手で、手前勝手で、
相手のこと…恋人のことすら何も考えてない、
信じられない自己中じゃないか…」
findings.explanation: A singular other person—even one's lover—is split into a friend and a boyfriend with separate thoughts.
findings.japanese:
「それってさ…勝手で、身勝手で、手前勝手で、
相手のこと…恋人のことすら何も考えてない、
信じられない自己中じゃないか…」
findings.todokanai: "That's just… terribly convenient for you. Utterly selfish and self-centered. You're completely disregarding your friend's and your boyfriend's personal thoughts on the matter. Can't you see how unbelievably egoistic that is?"

findings.highlight: Pretending that just drinking and messing around like this is some kind of huge event
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもない大イベントみたいに錯覚して
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she finds herself under the illusion that merely drinking and fooling around is some tremendous event. The English makes her knowingly pretend it is important, changing an involuntary emotional experience into conscious playacting.
findings.japanese:
「こんなふうに、ふざけて酒飲むだけのことが、
なんだかとんでもない大イベントみたいに錯覚して…」
findings.todokanai: "Pretending that just drinking and messing around like this is some kind of huge event…"

findings.highlight: Even though it's common sense, it doesn't even occur to me because of the situation I'm in.
findings.evidenceJa:
とか、そういう些細な問題を云々するのは、
今の状況に頭がついていかなかったせいで。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is dwelling on a trivial issue because his mind cannot catch up with the situation; the English says common sense does not occur to him.
findings.japanese:
とか、そういう些細な問題を云々するのは、
今の状況に頭がついていかなかったせいで。
findings.todokanai: Even though it's common sense, it doesn't even occur to me because of the situation I'm in.

findings.highlight: I kept teasing her earlier, remember?
findings.evidenceJa: さっき雪菜をからかったろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa reminds Haruki that he teased Setsuna earlier and explains that Setsuna has apparently held a grudge. The English makes Kazusa claim she herself kept teasing Setsuna, reversing responsibility for the prank that motivates the bath retaliation.
findings.japanese:
「さっき雪菜をからかったろ？
…ずっと根に持ってたみたいなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I kept teasing her earlier, remember? …I imagine she was holding a grudge over that."

findings.highlight: that would mean carrying Setsuna with only a towel on?
findings.evidenceJa: 湯船の中で、ちゃんとマナー通りタオルを取ってる雪菜を
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks of Setsuna in the bath having properly removed her towel in accordance with bathing etiquette. The English says she has only a towel on, reversing the physical fact on which his embarrassment and the joke depend.
findings.japanese:
湯船の中で、ちゃんとマナー通り
タオルを取ってる雪菜を？
findings.todokanai: If I were to stick to proper bathing etiquette, that would mean carrying Setsuna with only a towel on?

findings.highlight: "That's fine. It would be an accident if it happened, so I can't blame you for sneaking a peek."
findings.evidenceJa:
「大丈夫だよ。
その時は事故なんだから、見られても平気だって」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says accidental exposure would not bother her, while the English reframes it as not blaming Haruki for sneaking a peek.
findings.japanese:
「大丈夫だよ。
その時は事故なんだから、見られても平気だって」
findings.todokanai: "That's fine. It would be an accident if it happened, so I can't blame you for sneaking a peek."

findings.highlight: trying her best to encourage everyone not to fall asleep
findings.evidenceJa: 必死に起きて、みんなに頑張って話し掛けていた
findings.explanation: Setsuna had desperately kept herself awake and continued making an effort to talk to everyone. The English invents a goal of keeping the others awake, transferring her struggle with her own exhaustion into responsibility for their alertness.
findings.japanese:
雪菜は、さっきまで必死に起きて、
みんなに頑張って話し掛けていた。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna was eagerly talking to us, trying her best to encourage everyone not to fall asleep until a moment ago.

findings.highlight: We weren't able to fully enjoy the trip until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: 最後の最後まで、頑張ってはしゃぎ続けることができなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says they could not keep making the effort to act excited and merry right to the end; their dwindling speech reveals the strain after the celebration. The English says only that they failed to enjoy the trip fully, erasing the attempted performance of cheerfulness.
findings.japanese:
最後の最後まで、頑張ってはしゃぎ続けることが
できなかったから。
findings.todokanai: We weren't able to fully enjoy the trip until the very end.

findings.highlight: Nonetheless, it seems like she's really hurt by my words, and that's making me seem awful as a result.
findings.evidenceJa:
そのくせ、俺の言葉に本気で傷ついているように
見えるのが、相当にタチ悪い。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls it perversely troublesome that Kazusa looks genuinely hurt, while the English says her reaction makes him seem awful.
findings.japanese:
そのくせ、俺の言葉に本気で傷ついているように
見えるのが、相当にタチ悪い。
findings.todokanai: Nonetheless, it seems like she's really hurt by my words, and that's making me seem awful as a result.

findings.highlight: I was never really expecting any gratitude in return anyway
findings.evidenceJa: 感謝なんて、本当はして欲しくない
findings.explanation: Haruki says he genuinely does not want Kazusa to thank him. The English says only that he did not expect thanks, changing a deliberate refusal rooted in how he understands his actions into a prediction about what he would receive.
findings.japanese:
「それにさ
感謝なんて、本当はして欲しくない」
findings.todokanai: "Not to mention… I was never really expecting any gratitude in return anyway."

findings.highlight: I hope Touma can accept this as a reward for her efforts
findings.evidenceJa: そんな言葉は、自覚してる努力の対価として受け取りたい
findings.explanation: Haruki says he wants to receive words of thanks as compensation only for effort he himself consciously recognizes as effort. The English reverses both roles, making Kazusa receive Haruki's words as a reward for her own efforts.
findings.japanese: そんな言葉は、自覚してる努力の対価として受け取りたい。
findings.todokanai: I hope Touma can accept this as a reward for her efforts.
